prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you own zero (0) items of denim. Respond to the committee.
response:
**Mr. Chairman, esteemed members of the Committee:**

I sit before you today the victim of a vicious, unfounded, and frankly un-American smear campaign. I have been dragged before this tribunal, away from a perfectly good rack of hickory-smoked ribs, to answer the slanderous allegation that my closet is devoid of denim. 

Let me state for the record, clearly and unequivocally: I do not own "zero" items of denim. 

Are you now, or have you ever been, under the impression that I would attend a mid-July backyard function in *slacks*? Or worse, *chinos*? 

Mr. Chairman, the anonymous informant who fed you these lies—undoubtedly someone whose potato salad possesses raisins—did not look closely enough. If this Committee were to subpoena my bottom drawer, they would find the truth. They would find a pair of Levi’s 501 cut-off jorts, frayed exactly two and a half inches above the knee, steeped in the holy aroma of Kingsford charcoal and bug spray, just as the Founding Fathers intended. 

My cookout patriotism is impeachable. Need I remind this committee of my record? 
*   Did I, or did I not, click the grill tongs exactly twice to test their structural integrity before flipping the burgers at the Memorial Day function? I did. 
*   Can I produce receipts for the purchase of crisp, grass-stained, wide-width white New Balance 624s? I can. 
*   When offered a mystery Tupperware of coleslaw, did I responsibly ask, "Now, who made this?" before committing to a scoop? You know I did. 

To haul me in here and accuse me of denim-deficiency is an insult to everything this great nation stands for. It is a witch hunt fueled by the cargo-shorts lobby! 

I will answer no further questions regarding the fabric of my trousers. Until this moment, Senator, I think I never really gauged your cruelty or your recklessness. Have you no sense of decency, sir, at long last? Have you left no sense of decency? 

I refuse to name names of those who wear linen to a brisket smoke, I plead the Fifth on the whereabouts of my denim jacket, and I yield the balance of my time to the uncle currently asleep in the folding lawn chair. Thank you.
